sources.entry: Leon - Personal assistant who can live on your server. (Source Code) MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Leon is an open-source, self-hostable personal AI assistant built around tools, context, memory, and agentic execution, currently in a 2.0 Developer Preview.
summary.what_it_does: Leon runs in three modes: smart (chooses automatically), controlled (deterministic native skills and actions), and agent (step-by-step planning). It supports native skills and SKILL.md-based agent skills, organized as Skills, Actions, Tools, Functions and Binaries. The README describes computer use that can operate desktop and browser interfaces, locally or through Satellite. It keeps layered memory for preferences, daily context and recent discussion, and supports both local and remote AI providers. The repo includes toolkits for search, productivity, system utilities, media, coding assistance, and voice/audio. The README says it runs locally by default and includes a setup check command.
use_cases: run a private assistant on your own machine or server
automate tasks with tools and agent skills
desktop and browser automation with an AI agent
local AI model assistant with memory
how_to_run: git clone the repository and cd leon
notable: Privacy-focused: can work with local models and local context
Three execution modes: smart, controlled, and agent
Layered memory for durable preferences, daily context and recent discussion
Native skills plus SKILL.md-backed agent skills
Progressively loaded computer use for desktop and browser interfaces
caveats: Currently a 2.0 Developer Preview on the develop branch; the new documentation is not ready yet and the docs site mostly reflects legacy architecture
Legacy, more stable pre-agentic version is on the master branch
Contributor onboarding is progressive and the project is largely developed in spare time
